expected_level_description: You can: - listen to the needs of design and business stakeholders and interpret information - take part in discussions within a multidisciplinary team - be an advocate for the team externally, and can manage differing perspectives - shape and share communications relevant to the audience

You can: - provide advice, guidance and recommendations based on your specialist knowledge and experience - propose methodologies to follow and approaches to implementation - frame problems so they can easily be understood, and troubleshoot where required, to support the business in operating more effectively
You can: - analyse and provide feedback on governance and project documents, and on governance boards, according to a predefined framework, assessing them against accessibility standards

You can: - contribute to best practice guidelines - understand the sustainability and consequences of your decisions and can make decisions characterised by managed levels of risk and complexity - resolve technical disputes between wider peers and indirect stakeholders, taking into account all views and opinions

You can: - demonstrate knowledge and communicate the requirements of accessibility standards and legislation - advocate appropriate technical solutions to a range of accessibility issues - perform detailed audits of websites, services and documents, and document findings clearly for others to work from - be an advocate for the people affected by accessibility barriers across the department - provide introductory awareness and training about accessibility - demonstrate confidence using one or more assistive technologies, and knowledge of others
You can: - review requirements and specifications, and define test conditions - identify issues and risks associated with work - analyse and report test activities and results

You can: - identify and engage with users or stakeholders to collate user needs evidence - understand and define research that fits user needs - use quantitative and qualitative data about users to turn user focus into outcomes

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - carry out equality impact assessments - build inclusive teams and practices
You can: - explain how health IT systems can harm patients, for example through wrong, missing, or delayed information - report a possible clinical safety issue through the right route

skill: Designing for clinical safety and human factors
expected_level_description: You can: - explain how design choices can cause or prevent errors in care, such as wrong-patient or wrong-dose mistakes - use the organisation's patterns for safety-critical information, such as patient identity banners and allergy warnings
You can: - explain why health information must be accurate, current, and easy to understand - follow the team's style guide and clinical review process for health content
